name: Routine
author: Ricardo Liberato
description: How long until the next meeting, and what today is holding — from Routine, without opening it

barWidget.description: Counts down to the next event and opens today's agenda; needs the rtn CLI

schema.label: Path to rtn
schema.description: Left as a bare name it is resolved on PATH — which the graphical session does not always inherit the way a terminal does. If the widget says the binary is missing while a terminal finds it fine, put the absolute path here.

schema.label: Refresh every (seconds)
schema.description: How often to ask Routine. A call is a local memory read costing about ten milliseconds, so this is cheap — but the countdown itself ticks locally between polls and does not need one.

schema.label: Go urgent within (minutes)
schema.description: How close the next event has to be before the widget takes the urgent colour. Zero never does.

schema.label: Agent for Tab-to-ask
schema.description: Left empty this follows Omarchy's own `omarchy default agent`. rtn can currently drive claude headlessly; other agents take their MCP servers from persistent config rather than per invocation, so pointing one at Routine is a different setup and is not done for you.

schema.label: Model for Tab-to-ask
schema.description: Empty uses the agent's own default. `haiku` answers a question about today in about six seconds for a few cents; a larger model is slower and dearer for the same answer.
